chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Mufazzal ibn Salih, from Lays Al-Murady, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Masjid Al-Fadikh, why was it named Masjid Al-Fadikh? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Because of a palm tree named Al-Fadikh, therefore it was named Masjid Al-Fadikh.'

key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الْفَضِيخِ: Masjid Al-Fadikh (The Mosque of the Palm Tree)

ai.seo_question: Why is the mosque known as Masjid Al-Fadikh?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that Masjid Al-Fadikh was named after a specific palm tree known as 'Al-Fadikh' located there, highlighting the historical and geographical naming conventions of early Islamic shrines. This etymological detail underscores the organic development of sacred sites in Shia tradition, where natural landmarks often served as identifiers for places of worship and pilgrimage before formal architectural structures were established.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Mufazzal Bin Salih, from Lays Al Murady who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about Masjid Al-Fazeekh, ‘Why was it named as Masjid Al-Fazeekh?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Due to a palm tree named as Al-Fazeekh, so due to that it was named as Masjid Al-Fazeekh’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Layth al-Muradiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Why Masjid of al-Fadikh is called Masjid of al- Fadikh?’ He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is because of a palm tree that was called al-Fadikh and for this reason it is called Masjid of al-Fadikh.’”
